claim: In CMV-seropositive healthy adults, chronic CMV infection is associated with the expansion of perforin+/granzyme B+ CD4 T cells.
source: In healthy humans, chronic CMV infection is associated with the expansion of perforin+/granzyme B+ CD4 (Figure 1a–b and Figure 1—source data 1) (van Leeuwen et al., 2004).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1a-b and cited literature (van Leeuwen et al., 2004).

claim: High perforin expression is observed in terminally differentiated CD4 T cells that have downregulated CD28.
source: As previously reported, high perforin expression was observed in terminally differentiated CD4 and CD8 T cells that had downregulated the co-stimulatory molecules CD28 and CD27, respectively (Figure 1c) (van de Berg et al., 2008; Appay et al., 2002b).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data in Figure 1c and cited literature.

claim: Perforin+ CD4 T cells are CD8β-negative.
source: Perforin+ CD4 T cells were CD8β-negative and a minority expressed low levels of CD8α (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–b).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: A minority of perforin+ CD4 T cells express low levels of CD8α.
source: Perforin+ CD4 T cells were CD8β-negative and a minority expressed low levels of CD8α (Figure 1—figure supplement 1a–b).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: CD28- CD4 T cells show increased PRF1 gene expression compared to naive CD4 T cells.
source: Increased PRF1 gene expression by CD28- CD4 and CD27- CD8 T cells was confirmed by mRNA quantification and was associated with potent cytotoxic activity in a polyclonal cell lysis assay (Figure 1e, Figure 1f and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: CD28- CD4 T cells exhibit potent cytotoxic activity in a polyclonal cell lysis assay.
source: Increased PRF1 gene expression by CD28- CD4 and CD27- CD8 T cells was confirmed by mRNA quantification and was associated with potent cytotoxic activity in a polyclonal cell lysis assay (Figure 1e, Figure 1f and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 1f.

claim: The cytotoxic activity of CD28- CD4 T cells is abolished by Concanamycin A.
source: This activity was abolished by Concanamycin A, supporting a perforin-dependent mechanism (Kataoka et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is supported by experimental data showing loss of cytotoxicity with Concanamycin A treatment and cited literature.

claim: The cytotoxic activity of CD28- CD4 T cells is mediated by a perforin-dependent mechanism.
source: This activity was abolished by Concanamycin A, supporting a perforin-dependent mechanism (Kataoka et al., 1996).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the abolishment of cytotoxicity by Concanamycin A, a perforin inhibitor, and supported by cited literature.

claim: There is an inverse correlation between PRF1 gene expression and DNA methylation status of its promoter region.
source: Bisulphite sequencing indicated an inverse correlation between the expression of the PRF1 gene and the DNA methylation status of its promoter region (Figure 1g and Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: The PRF1 promoter is hypermethylated in the HEL-299 fibroblastic cell line.
source: Whereas PRF1 promoter was hypermethylated in a perforin- fibroblastic cell line (HEL-299), all CpG sites were hypomethylated in CD28- CD4 and CD27- CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: All CpG sites in the PRF1 promoter are hypomethylated in CD28- CD4 T cells.
source: Whereas PRF1 promoter was hypermethylated in a perforin- fibroblastic cell line (HEL-299), all CpG sites were hypomethylated in CD28- CD4 and CD27- CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: All CpG sites in the PRF1 promoter are hypomethylated in CD27- CD8 T cells.
source: Whereas PRF1 promoter was hypermethylated in a perforin- fibroblastic cell line (HEL-299), all CpG sites were hypomethylated in CD28- CD4 and CD27- CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Low DNA methylation levels are detected at intermediate CpG sites (16 to 28) in naive CD8 T cells.
source: Low DNA methylation levels were detected at intermediate (16 to 28; middle grey line on Figure 1g) CpG sites in naive CD8 T cells and at proximal (CpG sites 29 to 34; right grey line) sites in both naive CD4 and CD8 T cells, suggesting that the PRF1 gene is transcriptionally poised in naive T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Low DNA methylation levels are detected at proximal CpG sites (29 to 34) in naive CD4 T cells.
source: Low DNA methylation levels were detected at intermediate (16 to 28; middle grey line on Figure 1g) CpG sites in naive CD8 T cells and at proximal (CpG sites 29 to 34; right grey line) sites in both naive CD4 and CD8 T cells, suggesting that the PRF1 gene is transcriptionally poised in naive T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: Low DNA methylation levels are detected at proximal CpG sites (29 to 34) in naive CD8 T cells.
source: Low DNA methylation levels were detected at intermediate (16 to 28; middle grey line on Figure 1g) CpG sites in naive CD8 T cells and at proximal (CpG sites 29 to 34; right grey line) sites in both naive CD4 and CD8 T cells, suggesting that the PRF1 gene is transcriptionally poised in naive T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite sequencing data shown in Figure 1g.

claim: The PRF1 gene is transcriptionally poised in naive T lymphocytes.
source: Low DNA methylation levels were detected at intermediate (16 to 28; middle grey line on Figure 1g) CpG sites in naive CD8 T cells and at proximal (CpG sites 29 to 34; right grey line) sites in both naive CD4 and CD8 T cells, suggesting that the PRF1 gene is transcriptionally poised in naive T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the low methylation levels at specific CpG sites in naive T cells.

claim: CD28- CD4 T cells exert a cytotoxic activity comparable to CD27- CD8 T cells.
source: Together, these results indicate that CD28- CD4 T cells exert a cytotoxic activity comparable to CD27- CD8 T cells and that this subset can therefore be used as a relevant model of in vivo differentiated CD4CTX T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by the cytotoxicity assay data presented in Figure 1f.

claim: Naive and cytotoxic T cells form separate clusters in unsupervised transcriptome analysis.
source: Unsupervised analysis of transcriptional programs indicated that naive and cytotoxic T cells formed separate clusters and that CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells were more closely related than their naive counterparts (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: The claim is supported by unsupervised clustering analysis shown in Figure 2a-b.

claim: CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells are more closely related transcriptionally than their naive counterparts.
source: Unsupervised analysis of transcriptional programs indicated that naive and cytotoxic T cells formed separate clusters and that CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells were more closely related than their naive counterparts (Figure 2a–b).
evidence: The claim is supported by unsupervised clustering and principal component analyses shown in Figure 2a-b.

claim: Genes upregulated in CD8CTX T cells are significantly enriched in genes of the CD8 T cell lineage.
source: As expected, genes that were upregulated in CD8CTX T cells were significantly enriched in genes of the CD8 T cell lineage (Figure 2c).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claim: Genes upregulated in CD4CTX T cells are enriched in CD8 rather than CD4 T cell lineage genes.
source: Strikingly, genes upregulated in CD4CTX T cells were also enriched in CD8 rather than CD4 T cell lineage genes.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2c.

claim: The transcriptional program common to CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells includes RUNX3, TBX21 (T-bet) and EOMES.
source: The transcriptional program common to CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells included RUNX3, TBX21 (T-bet) and EOMES, TF known to promote effector and memory functions in CD8 T cells (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2d and Figure 2—source data 1) (Cruz-Guilloty et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2d and Supplementary file 1, and cited literature.

claim: RUNX3, TBX21 (T-bet) and EOMES are transcription factors known to promote effector and memory functions in CD8 T cells.
source: The transcriptional program common to CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells included RUNX3, TBX21 (T-bet) and EOMES, TF known to promote effector and memory functions in CD8 T cells (Supplementary file 1, Figure 2d and Figure 2—source data 1) (Cruz-Guilloty et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Cruz-Guilloty et al., 2009).

claim: The enrichment in CD8 T cell lineage genes by CD4CTX T cells is not associated with the downregulation of ZBTB7B (ThPOK).
source: Strikingly, the enrichment in CD8 T cell lineage genes by CD4CTX T cells was not associated with the downregulation of ZBTB7B (ThPOK) (Figure 2d and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: ThPOK expression is higher in naive CD4 T cells compared to naive CD8 T cells.
source: As expected, ThPOK expression was higher in naive CD4 as compared to naive CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2d and is consistent with established knowledge.

claim: ThPOK gene expression is not downregulated by human circulating CD4CTX T cells.
source: However, in contrast to mouse intestinal CD4 T cells (Mucida et al., 2013), ThPOK gene expression was not downregulated by human circulating CD4 T cells, CD4CTX T cells expressing higher levels of ThPOK mRNA than naive CD4 T cells (Figure 2d and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2d and contrasts with cited literature on mouse cells.

claim: CD4CTX T cells express higher levels of ThPOK mRNA than naive CD4 T cells.
source: However, in contrast to mouse intestinal CD4 T cells (Mucida et al., 2013), ThPOK gene expression was not downregulated by human circulating CD4 T cells, CD4CTX T cells expressing higher levels of ThPOK mRNA than naive CD4 T cells (Figure 2d and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 2d.

claim: Protein expression analysis confirms mRNA expression profiles for Runx3, T-bet and Eomes.
source: Protein expression analysis by flow cytometry confirmed mRNA expression profiles for Runx3, T-bet and Eomes (Figure 2e and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: CD4CTX and naive CD4 T cells show high and similar expression of ThPOK protein.
source: This analysis showed high and similar expression of ThPOK in CD4CTX and naive CD4 T cells and a higher expression of ThPOK in CD8CTX as compared to naive CD8 T cells (Figure 2e and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: CD8CTX T cells show higher expression of ThPOK protein compared to naive CD8 T cells.
source: This analysis showed high and similar expression of ThPOK in CD4CTX and naive CD4 T cells and a higher expression of ThPOK in CD8CTX as compared to naive CD8 T cells (Figure 2e and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2e.

claim: The acquisition of cytotoxic function by CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells is associated with changes in methylation, primarily hypomethylation, of large numbers of genes.
source: The acquisition of cytotoxic function by CD4CTX and CD8CTX T cells was associated with changes in methylation, primarily hypomethylation, of large numbers of genes (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation array data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-d.

claim: Naive and cytotoxic T cells form separate clusters in unsupervised DNA methylome analysis.
source: Unsupervised analysis of DNA methylomes indicated that naive and cytotoxic T cells formed separate clusters (Figure 2—figure supplement 1e).
evidence: The claim is supported by unsupervised clustering analysis of methylation data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1e.

claim: Genes expressed at higher levels in CD4CTX T cells compared to naive counterparts are significantly enriched in hypomethylated CpG located in their promoter regions.
source: GSEA indicated that genes expressed at higher levels in CD4CTX or CD8CTX T cells as compared to their naive counterparts were significantly enriched in hypomethylated CpG located in their promoter regions (Figure 2f).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Genes expressed at higher levels in CD8CTX T cells compared to naive counterparts are significantly enriched in hypomethylated CpG located in their promoter regions.
source: GSEA indicated that genes expressed at higher levels in CD4CTX or CD8CTX T cells as compared to their naive counterparts were significantly enriched in hypomethylated CpG located in their promoter regions (Figure 2f).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Genes downregulated in CD4CTX T cells are not enriched in hypermethylated CpG.
source: In contrast, genes that were downregulated in CD4CTX or CD8CTX T cells were not enriched in hypermethylated CpG, suggesting distinct epigenetic mechanisms in the up- and downregulation of genes upon differentiation of cytotoxic T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Genes downregulated in CD8CTX T cells are not enriched in hypermethylated CpG.
source: In contrast, genes that were downregulated in CD4CTX or CD8CTX T cells were not enriched in hypermethylated CpG, suggesting distinct epigenetic mechanisms in the up- and downregulation of genes upon differentiation of cytotoxic T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 2f.

claim: Distinct epigenetic mechanisms are involved in the up- and downregulation of genes upon differentiation of cytotoxic T cells.
source: In contrast, genes that were downregulated in CD4CTX or CD8CTX T cells were not enriched in hypermethylated CpG, suggesting distinct epigenetic mechanisms in the up- and downregulation of genes upon differentiation of cytotoxic T cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential enrichment patterns of hypomethylated vs hypermethylated CpG in up- vs downregulated genes.

claim: RUNX3 promoter shows significant hypomethylation in CD4CTX T cells compared to naive CD4 T cells.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of TF up regulated in cytotoxic as compared to naive T cells suggested significant hypomethylation for RUNX3 and TBX21 in both CD4CTX and CD8CTX (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1), but not for EOMES (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: TBX21 promoter shows significant hypomethylation in CD4CTX T cells compared to naive CD4 T cells.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of TF up regulated in cytotoxic as compared to naive T cells suggested significant hypomethylation for RUNX3 and TBX21 in both CD4CTX and CD8CTX (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1), but not for EOMES (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: RUNX3 promoter shows significant hypomethylation in CD8CTX T cells compared to naive CD8 T cells.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of TF up regulated in cytotoxic as compared to naive T cells suggested significant hypomethylation for RUNX3 and TBX21 in both CD4CTX and CD8CTX (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1), but not for EOMES (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: TBX21 promoter shows significant hypomethylation in CD8CTX T cells compared to naive CD8 T cells.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of TF up regulated in cytotoxic as compared to naive T cells suggested significant hypomethylation for RUNX3 and TBX21 in both CD4CTX and CD8CTX (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1), but not for EOMES (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: EOMES promoter does not show significant hypomethylation in cytotoxic T cells compared to naive T cells.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of TF up regulated in cytotoxic as compared to naive T cells suggested significant hypomethylation for RUNX3 and TBX21 in both CD4CTX and CD8CTX (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1), but not for EOMES (data not shown).
evidence: The claim is stated explicitly in the text.

claim: ZBTB7B promoter is significantly hypomethylated in naive CD4 T cells compared to naive CD8 T cells.
source: As observed during thymopoiesis (Vacchio and Bosselut, 2016), ZBTB7B promoter was significantly hypomethylated in naive CD4 as compared to naive CD8 T cells, but no significant difference was observed between CD4CTX and CD8CTX cells (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 2g and cited literature.

claim: No significant difference in ZBTB7B promoter methylation is observed between CD4CTX and CD8CTX cells.
source: As observed during thymopoiesis (Vacchio and Bosselut, 2016), ZBTB7B promoter was significantly hypomethylated in naive CD4 as compared to naive CD8 T cells, but no significant difference was observed between CD4CTX and CD8CTX cells (Figure 2g and Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: Most analyzed RUNX3 probes (77%) are located in the distal promoter (TSS1500).
source: Most analyzed RUNX3 probes (77%) were located in the distal promoter (TSS1500), a region suspected to be involved in the control of RUNX3 mRNA translation (Kim et al., 2015), whereas most TBX21 (77%) and ZBTB7B probes (76%) were located in the proximal promoter (5'UTR, 1st exon and TSS200).
evidence: The claim is stated explicitly and references cited literature about the distal promoter region.

claim: The distal promoter region (TSS1500) of RUNX3 is suspected to be involved in the control of RUNX3 mRNA translation.
source: Most analyzed RUNX3 probes (77%) were located in the distal promoter (TSS1500), a region suspected to be involved in the control of RUNX3 mRNA translation (Kim et al., 2015), whereas most TBX21 (77%) and ZBTB7B probes (76%) were located in the proximal promoter (5'UTR, 1st exon and TSS200).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (Kim et al., 2015).

claim: Most TBX21 probes (77%) are located in the proximal promoter (5'UTR, 1st exon and TSS200).
source: Most analyzed RUNX3 probes (77%) were located in the distal promoter (TSS1500), a region suspected to be involved in the control of RUNX3 mRNA translation (Kim et al., 2015), whereas most TBX21 (77%) and ZBTB7B probes (76%) were located in the proximal promoter (5'UTR, 1st exon and TSS200).
evidence: The claim is stated explicitly in the text.

claim: Most ZBTB7B probes (76%) are located in the proximal promoter (5'UTR, 1st exon and TSS200).
source: Most analyzed RUNX3 probes (77%) were located in the distal promoter (TSS1500), a region suspected to be involved in the control of RUNX3 mRNA translation (Kim et al., 2015), whereas most TBX21 (77%) and ZBTB7B probes (76%) were located in the proximal promoter (5'UTR, 1st exon and TSS200).
evidence: The claim is stated explicitly in the text.

claim: The transcriptional program of human CD4CTX T cells is enriched in CD8 T cell lineage genes.
source: Together, these results indicate that the transcriptional program of human CD4CTX T cells is enriched in CD8 T cell lineage genes.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the GSEA and gene expression analyses presented.

claim: Acquisition of the CD8 T cell lineage gene program by CD4CTX T cells involves extensive hypomethylation of the promoter regions of a large number of genes, including transcription factors.
source: Acquisition of this program involves extensive hypomethylation of the promoter regions of a large number of genes, including TF, and is not accompanied by ThPOK downregulation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the DNA methylation analyses presented.

claim: Acquisition of the CD8 T cell lineage gene program by CD4CTX T cells is not accompanied by ThPOK downregulation.
source: Acquisition of this program involves extensive hypomethylation of the promoter regions of a large number of genes, including TF, and is not accompanied by ThPOK downregulation.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the gene expression and protein analyses presented.

claim: The production of perforin is associated with the expression of the Th1 chemokine receptors CCR5 and, to a lower extent, CXCR3.
source: The production of perforin was associated with the expression of the Th1 chemokine receptors CCR5 and, to a lower extend, CXCR3 but not with Th17 or Th2 receptors CCR6, CCR4 or CRTh2 (Figure 3a). (Sallusto et al., 1998; Cosmi et al., 2000; Rivino et al., 2004; Cohen et al., 2011; Couturier et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3a and cited literature.

claim: The production of perforin is not associated with Th17 or Th2 receptors CCR6, CCR4 or CRTh2.
source: The production of perforin was associated with the expression of the Th1 chemokine receptors CCR5 and, to a lower extend, CXCR3 but not with Th17 or Th2 receptors CCR6, CCR4 or CRTh2 (Figure 3a). (Sallusto et al., 1998; Cosmi et al., 2000; Rivino et al., 2004; Cohen et al., 2011; Couturier et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3a and cited literature.

claim: No perforin+ cells are detected by flow cytometry among central memory (CM) CD4 T cells.
source: No perforin+ cells were detected by flow cytometry among CM CD4 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3b-c.

claim: A small proportion of perforin+ cells are detected among CD28+ effector memory (EM) CD4 T cells in some donors.
source: A small proportion of perforin+ cells were detected among CD28+ EM CD4 T cells in some donors and these cells were CCR5+.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3b-c.

claim: Perforin+ cells among CD28+ effector memory (EM) CD4 T cells are CCR5+.
source: A small proportion of perforin+ cells were detected among CD28+ EM CD4 T cells in some donors and these cells were CCR5+.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3b.

claim: CD4CTX cells show high perforin expression by mean fluorescence intensity analysis.
source: Mean fluorescence intensity analysis indicated high perforin expression by CD4CTX cells and low and comparable expression in naive, CCR5+ CM (CMTh1) and CCR5+ CD28+ EM (EM28+Th1) CD4 T cells (Figure 3c and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: Naive, CCR5+ CM (CMTh1) and CCR5+ CD28+ EM (EM28+Th1) CD4 T cells show low and comparable perforin expression by mean fluorescence intensity analysis.
source: Mean fluorescence intensity analysis indicated high perforin expression by CD4CTX cells and low and comparable expression in naive, CCR5+ CM (CMTh1) and CCR5+ CD28+ EM (EM28+Th1) CD4 T cells (Figure 3c and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 3c.

claim: PRF1 gene is expressed at higher levels in CMTh1 cells compared to naive CD4 T cells.
source: In contrast, PRF1 mRNA expression analysis of sorted cells (sorting strategy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) indicated that the PRF1 gene was already expressed at higher levels in CMTh1 as compared to naive cells and was further upregulated in EM28+Th1 cells and in CD4CTX cells (Figure 3d and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: PRF1 gene expression is further upregulated in EM28+Th1 cells compared to CMTh1 cells.
source: In contrast, PRF1 mRNA expression analysis of sorted cells (sorting strategy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) indicated that the PRF1 gene was already expressed at higher levels in CMTh1 as compared to naive cells and was further upregulated in EM28+Th1 cells and in CD4CTX cells (Figure 3d and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: PRF1 gene expression is further upregulated in CD4CTX cells compared to EM28+Th1 cells.
source: In contrast, PRF1 mRNA expression analysis of sorted cells (sorting strategy shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1a) indicated that the PRF1 gene was already expressed at higher levels in CMTh1 as compared to naive cells and was further upregulated in EM28+Th1 cells and in CD4CTX cells (Figure 3d and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The pattern of progressive upregulation of gene expression from naive to CMTh1 to EM28+Th1 to CD4CTX cells is similar for RUNX3 and TBX21.
source: Notably, this pattern of progressive up regulation of gene expression was similar for RUNX3 and TBX21 and contrasted with the high expression of IFNG and EOMES mRNA already detected at the CMTh1 stage of differentiation (Figure 3d, and Figure 3—source data 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: IFNG mRNA is expressed at high levels already at the CMTh1 stage of differentiation.
source: Notably, this pattern of progressive up regulation of gene expression was similar for RUNX3 and TBX21 and contrasted with the high expression of IFNG and EOMES mRNA already detected at the CMTh1 stage of differentiation (Figure 3d, and Figure 3—source data 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: EOMES mRNA is expressed at high levels already at the CMTh1 stage of differentiation.
source: Notably, this pattern of progressive up regulation of gene expression was similar for RUNX3 and TBX21 and contrasted with the high expression of IFNG and EOMES mRNA already detected at the CMTh1 stage of differentiation (Figure 3d, and Figure 3—source data 1 and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3d.

claim: The increased expression of perforin and associated transcription factors is specific to the Th1 lineage.
source: Analysis of sorted CM Th1, Th2 and Th17 cells indicated that the increased expression of perforin and associated TF was specific to the Th1 lineage (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b–c).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b-c.

claim: DNA methylation levels at intermediate CpGs (sites 16 to 28) of the PRF1 promoter progressively decrease from naive to CMTh1, EM28+Th1 and CD4CTX T cells.
source: Epigenetic analyses of the PRF1 promoter further supported the stepwise acquisition of perforin expression within the Th1 lineage. DNA methylation levels at intermediate CpGs (sites 16 to 28) progressively decreased from naive to CMTh1, EM28+Th1 and CD4CTX T cells (Figure 3e and Supplementary file 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite pyrosequencing data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: Proximal CpGs (sites 29 to 34) of the PRF1 promoter are hypomethylated in CMTh1 and CD28+ EMTh1 T cells.
source: As observed in naive and CD4CTX T cells, proximal CpGs (sites 29 to 34) were hypomethylated in CMTh1 and CD28+ EMTh1 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by bisulfite pyrosequencing data shown in Figure 3e.

claim: High enrichment of H3K4me3 is detected at the PRF1 proximal promoter region in CD4CTX T cells.
source: In agreement with PRF1 gene expression and promoter methylation, high enrichment of H3K4me3 and of H3K27ac was detected at the PRF1 proximal promoter region in CD4CTX T cells (Figure 3f, middle and right panels and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: High enrichment of H3K27ac is detected at the PRF1 proximal promoter region in CD4CTX T cells.
source: In agreement with PRF1 gene expression and promoter methylation, high enrichment of H3K4me3 and of H3K27ac was detected at the PRF1 proximal promoter region in CD4CTX T cells (Figure 3f, middle and right panels and Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 3f.

claim: An H3K27ac enrichment is observed in a region located 5.5 to 7.7 kb upstream of the TSS in Th1 cell subsets, suggesting the presence of an active enhancer.
source: Interestingly, an H3K27ac enrichment was observed in a region located 5,5 to 7,7 kb upstream of the TSS in Th1 cell subsets, suggesting the presence of an active enhancer.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the H3K27ac enrichment pattern shown in Figure 3f, as H3K27ac marks active enhancers.

claim: The acquisition of PRF1 gene expression in vivo is related to a progressive increase in the proportion of PRF1 mRNA+ Th1 cells.
source: Together, these results indicate the progressive acquisition of PRF1 gene expression from CMTh1 to EMTh1 lymphocytes. Single-cell PCR analysis revealed that this process is related to a progressive increase in the proportion of PRF1 mRNA+ Th1 cells (Figure 4a and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: In CMTh1 cells, PRF1 expression is co-expressed with a relatively restricted set of transcription factors, including PRDM1, RUNX3 and EOMES.
source: Gene co-expression analysis at the single-cell level indicated that PRF1 mRNA was co-expressed with distinct sets of TF in Th1 cell subsets (Figure 4b and Figure 4—source data 1). In CMTh1 cells, PRF1 expression was co-expressed with a relatively restricted set of TF, including PRDM1, RUNX3 and EOMES.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: In CD4CTX T cells, PRF1 is co-expressed with a larger set of transcription factors including TBX21, HOPX, ZNF683 (Hobit), PRDM1, RUNX3 and EOMES.
source: In CD4CTX T cells, a larger set of co-expressed TF was identified, including TBX21, HOPX, ZNF683 (Hobit), PRDM1 and RUNX3 and EOMES.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: A lower proportion of perforin+ CD4CTX T cells co-express EOMES compared to the other co-expressed transcription factors.
source: Notably, a lower proportion of perforin+ CD4CTX T cells co-expressed EOMES as compared to the other co-expressed TF.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell qPCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Th1 lymphocytes acquire permissive modifications of the local chromatin environment that could underlie the acquisition of cytotoxic functions.
source: In conclusion, the analysis of PRF1 gene expression in vivo suggests a model in which Th1 lymphocytes acquire permissive modifications of the local chromatin environment and a network of TF factors that could underlie the acquisition of cytotoxic functions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the progressive epigenetic changes observed at the PRF1 locus.

claim: Th1 lymphocytes acquire a network of transcription factors that could underlie the acquisition of cytotoxic functions.
source: In conclusion, the analysis of PRF1 gene expression in vivo suggests a model in which Th1 lymphocytes acquire permissive modifications of the local chromatin environment and a network of TF factors that could underlie the acquisition of cytotoxic functions.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the progressive changes in transcription factor expression observed in Th1 cell subsets.

claim: CMTh1 cells form a cluster separated from naive and CD4CTX T cells in unsupervised gene expression analysis.
source: Unsupervised gene expression analysis indicated that CMTh1 cells formed a cluster separated from naive and CD4CTX T cells and were more closely related to CD4CTX T cells than to naive cells (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by unsupervised clustering analysis shown in Figure 5a.

claim: CMTh1 cells are more closely related to CD4CTX T cells than to naive cells in gene expression analysis.
source: Unsupervised gene expression analysis indicated that CMTh1 cells formed a cluster separated from naive and CD4CTX T cells and were more closely related to CD4CTX T cells than to naive cells (Figure 5a).
evidence: The claim is supported by unsupervised clustering analysis shown in Figure 5a.

claim: The transcriptome of CMTh1 cells is more distant to CD8CTX T cells than CD4CTX T cells.
source: Including CD8 T cell subsets in this analysis indicated that the transcriptome of CMTh1 cells was more distant to CD8CTX T cells than CD4CTX T cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 2a–b).
evidence: The claim is supported by unsupervised clustering and PCA analyses shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2a-b.

claim: 693 genes are significantly upregulated in CMTh1 cells compared to naive CD4 T cells.
source: 693 genes were significantly upregulated in CMTh1 as compared to naive cells and 322 genes were up regulated in CD4CTX T cells as compared to CMTh1 cells (Figure 5b and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: 322 genes are upregulated in CD4CTX T cells compared to CMTh1 cells.
source: 693 genes were significantly upregulated in CMTh1 as compared to naive cells and 322 genes were up regulated in CD4CTX T cells as compared to CMTh1 cells (Figure 5b and Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by differential gene expression analysis shown in Figure 5b.

claim: Genes upregulated in CD4CTX T cells compared to CMTh1 cells include cytotoxicity-related molecules such as GNLY (granulysin), granzymes, CD107a (LAMP1), CX3CR1 and CD8A.
source: As expected, genes upregulated in CD4CTX T cells as compared to CMTh1 cells included cytotoxicity-related molecules, among which GNLY (granulysin), granzymes, CD107a (LAMP1), CX3CR1 and CD8A as well as TF RUNX3 and EOMES (Figure 5c–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5c-d.

claim: Genes upregulated in CD4CTX T cells compared to CMTh1 cells include transcription factors RUNX3 and EOMES.
source: As expected, genes upregulated in CD4CTX T cells as compared to CMTh1 cells included cytotoxicity-related molecules, among which GNLY (granulysin), granzymes, CD107a (LAMP1), CX3CR1 and CD8A as well as TF RUNX3 and EOMES (Figure 5c–d).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 5c-d.

claim: T-bet is not upregulated in the transcriptome dataset comparing CD4CTX to CMTh1 cells, in line with reported lack of sensitivity of the Illumina array for this gene.
source: T-bet was not up regulated in the transcriptome dataset, in line with reported lack of sensitivity of the Illumina array for this gene (Dimova et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by the absence of T-bet upregulation in the array data and cited literature explaining technical limitations.

claim: Expression of IFNG, TNF and GZMK is increased in CMTh1 cells compared to naive cells but is not further upregulated in CD4CTX T cells.
source: Expression of IFNG, TNF and GZMK was increased in CMTh1 as compared to naive cells but was not further up regulated in CD4CTX T cells (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by gene expression data in Supplementary file 1.

claim: Gene upregulation in CMTh1 and CD4CTX T cells is primarily associated with DNA hypomethylation.
source: Methylome analysis indicated that gene up regulation in CMTh1 and CD4CTX T cells was primarily associated with DNA hypomethylation, as observed in the naive to CD4CTX T cell differentiation (Figure 5—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation array data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Effector molecules and receptors upregulated in CD4CTX cells are hypomethylated in their promoter regions.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of effector molecules and receptors and of TF upregulated in CD4CTX cells were also hypomethylated in these cells (Figure 5e–f and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 5e-f.

claim: Transcription factors upregulated in CD4CTX cells are hypomethylated in their promoter regions.
source: Analysis of probes located in the promoter region of effector molecules and receptors and of TF upregulated in CD4CTX cells were also hypomethylated in these cells (Figure 5e–f and Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by DNA methylation data shown in Figure 5e-f.

claim: Naive CD4 T cells stimulated in the presence of Th1 polarizing cytokines acquire cytotoxic function in vitro.
source: In line with our in vivo observations, cytotoxicity was acquired under Th1 and not under Th2 or Th17 culture conditions (Figure 6b to e and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro differentiation experiments shown in Figure 6b-e.

claim: Cytotoxicity is not acquired by naive CD4 T cells under Th2 culture conditions.
source: In line with our in vivo observations, cytotoxicity was acquired under Th1 and not under Th2 or Th17 culture conditions (Figure 6b to e and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro differentiation experiments shown in Figure 6b-e.

claim: Cytotoxicity is not acquired by naive CD4 T cells under Th17 culture conditions.
source: In line with our in vivo observations, cytotoxicity was acquired under Th1 and not under Th2 or Th17 culture conditions (Figure 6b to e and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by in vitro differentiation experiments shown in Figure 6b-e.

claim: In vitro differentiated Th1 cells include a diverse repertoire of clonotypes with similar proportions of large and intermediate expansions as compared to Th2 and Th17 cells.
source: In vitro differentiated Th1 cells included a diverse repertoire of clonotypes with similar proportions of large and intermediate expansions as compared to Th1 and Th2 cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: The claim is supported by TCR repertoire sequencing data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: In vitro differentiated Th1 cells express low levels of the PLZF transcription factor.
source: Furthermore, Th1 cells expressed low levels of the PLZF TF (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) indicating that they were conventional and not innate-type effector T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1b.

claim: In vitro differentiated Th1 cells are conventional and not innate-type effector T lymphocytes.
source: Furthermore, Th1 cells expressed low levels of the PLZF TF (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) indicating that they were conventional and not innate-type effector T lymphocytes.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the low PLZF expression, as PLZF is a marker of innate-like T cells.

claim: Frequencies of perforin+granzyme B+ cells increase from day 7 to day 21 in Th1 polarized cells.
source: Frequencies of perforin+granzyme B+ cells and levels of PRF1 mRNA increased from day 7 to day 21 in Th1 polarized cells (Figure 6b–c–e and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6b-c.

claim: Levels of PRF1 mRNA increase from day 7 to day 21 in Th1 polarized cells.
source: Frequencies of perforin+granzyme B+ cells and levels of PRF1 mRNA increased from day 7 to day 21 in Th1 polarized cells (Figure 6b–c–e and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: GNLY and TNF mRNA levels increase following a similar kinetics to PRF1 in Th1 polarized cells.
source: GNLY and TNF mRNA levels increased following a similar kinetics, whereas GZMB, IFNG and GZMK already reached maximum levels at day 7 (Figure 6e, Figure 6—figure supplement 2, and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6e and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: GZMB, IFNG and GZMK mRNA already reach maximum levels at day 7 in Th1 polarized cells.
source: GNLY and TNF mRNA levels increased following a similar kinetics, whereas GZMB, IFNG and GZMK already reached maximum levels at day 7 (Figure 6e, Figure 6—figure supplement 2, and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6e and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: CX3CR1 mRNA presents a unique expression profile with an initial upregulation followed by a marked downregulation in Th1 polarized cells.
source: CX3CR1 mRNA presented a unique expression profile with an initial upregulation followed by a marked downregulation (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2a.

claim: At day 14, Th1 polarized cells acquire potent Concanamycin A-sensitive cytotoxic activity.
source: At day 14, Th1 polarized cells acquired potent Concanamycin A-sensitive cytotoxic activity (Figure 6d and Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 6d.

claim: TBX21 and HOPX expression is specifically induced under Th1 conditions.
source: Most selected TF were induced by cell activation but their pattern of expression was differently associated with polarizing conditions (Figure 6e and Figure 6—source data 1). TBX21 and HOPX expression was specifically induced under Th1 conditions.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: RUNX3 and ZBTB7B mRNA are upregulated in all polarizing conditions but reach higher levels in Th1 cells.
source: RUNX3 and ZBTB7B mRNA were upregulated in all conditions but reached higher levels in Th1 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: EOMES is induced in both Th1 and Th2 cells.
source: EOMES was induced in both Th1 and Th2 cells, suggesting that expression of this TF is not sufficient to promote cytotoxic function in CD4 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Expression of EOMES is not sufficient to promote cytotoxic function in CD4 T cells.
source: EOMES was induced in both Th1 and Th2 cells, suggesting that expression of this TF is not sufficient to promote cytotoxic function in CD4 T cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that EOMES is expressed in Th2 cells which do not acquire cytotoxicity.

claim: ZNF683 mRNA is not detected in in vitro differentiated effector T cells.
source: The pattern of expression of ASCL2 and ZEB2 was inconsistent and ZNF683 mRNA was not detected in in vitro differentiated effector T cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2a.

claim: The expression of perforin is correlated with those of T-bet, Eomes, Runx3 and ThPOK in Th1 cells.
source: Flow cytometry analysis of Th1 cells indicated that the expression of perforin was correlated with those of T-bet, Eomes, Runx3 and ThPOK (Figure 6f and Figure 6—figure supplement 2b).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6f and Figure 6—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Knockdown of Runx3 results in decreased expression of perforin and granzyme B in Th1 cells.
source: Knockdown of Runx3 and, to a lesser extend, T-bet resulted in the decreased expression of perforin and granzyme B.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7b-d.

claim: Knockdown of T-bet results in decreased expression of perforin and granzyme B in Th1 cells, to a lesser extent than Runx3.
source: Knockdown of Runx3 and, to a lesser extend, T-bet resulted in the decreased expression of perforin and granzyme B.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7b-d.

claim: Knockdown of Hopx affects GZMB but not PRF1 mRNA expression in Th1 cells.
source: Knockdown of Hopx affected GZMB but not PRF1 mRNA expression, whereas knockdown of Eomes had no significant effect on the expression of either perforin or granzyme B (Figure 7b–d and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7b-d.

claim: Knockdown of Eomes has no significant effect on the expression of perforin or granzyme B in Th1 cells.
source: Knockdown of Hopx affected GZMB but not PRF1 mRNA expression, whereas knockdown of Eomes had no significant effect on the expression of either perforin or granzyme B (Figure 7b–d and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7b-d.

claim: IFNG expression is principally dependent on T-bet with no significant effect of Runx3 knockdown.
source: Of note, IFNG expression was principally dependent on T-bet with no significant effect of Runx3 knockdown (Figure 7b).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7b.

claim: T-bet controls TNF, CX3CR1 and GZMK expression in Th1 cells.
source: T-bet also controlled TNF, CX3CR1 and GZMK expression whereas GNLY was controlled by both Runx3 and T-bet (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claim: GNLY is controlled by both Runx3 and T-bet in Th1 cells.
source: T-bet also controlled TNF, CX3CR1 and GZMK expression whereas GNLY was controlled by both Runx3 and T-bet (Figure 7—figure supplement 1b).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1b.

claim: Runx3 and T-bet control the expression of HOPX in Th1 cells.
source: Significant interactions were observed between TF, with Runx3 and T-bet controlling the expression of HOPX and T-bet and Hopx controlling the expression of EOMES (Figure 7—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1c.

claim: T-bet and Hopx control the expression of EOMES in Th1 cells.
source: Significant interactions were observed between TF, with Runx3 and T-bet controlling the expression of HOPX and T-bet and Hopx controlling the expression of EOMES (Figure 7—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Runx3 significantly modulates the acquisition of cytotoxic activity by CD4 T cells.
source: In line with its central influence on the expression of cytotoxic molecules, Runx3 also significantly modulated the acquisition of cytotoxic activity by CD4 T cells, whereas T-bet knockdown reduced cytotoxicity of CD4 T cells only at low E/T ratios (Figure 7e and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: T-bet knockdown reduces cytotoxicity of CD4 T cells only at low effector/target ratios.
source: In line with its central influence on the expression of cytotoxic molecules, Runx3 also significantly modulated the acquisition of cytotoxic activity by CD4 T cells, whereas T-bet knockdown reduced cytotoxicity of CD4 T cells only at low E/T ratios (Figure 7e and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by cytotoxicity assay data shown in Figure 7e.

claim: ThPOK acts as a negative regulator of the cytotoxic program in CD4 T cells.
source: ThPOK globally acted as a negative regulator of the cytotoxic program (Figure 7f–g, Figure 7—figure supplement 1b–c and Figure 7—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7f-g and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b-c.

claim: ThPOK knockdown markedly increases PRF1 and GZMB expression in CD4 T cells.
source: ThPOK knockdown markedly increased PRF1 and GZMB expression and cytotoxic activity of CD4 T cells and also upregulated the expression of all the other TF studied and of CD8A.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7b-d and Figure 7f-g.

claim: ThPOK knockdown markedly increases cytotoxic activity of CD4 T cells.
source: ThPOK knockdown markedly increased PRF1 and GZMB expression and cytotoxic activity of CD4 T cells and also upregulated the expression of all the other TF studied and of CD8A.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7e.

claim: ThPOK knockdown upregulates the expression of all the other transcription factors studied and of CD8A in CD4 T cells.
source: ThPOK knockdown markedly increased PRF1 and GZMB expression and cytotoxic activity of CD4 T cells and also upregulated the expression of all the other TF studied and of CD8A.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7f-g and Figure 7—figure supplement 1b-c.

claim: In vitro activation of naive CD8 T cells induces the differentiation of perforin+ cells that co-express ThPOK.
source: In vitro activation of naive CD8 T cells induced the differentiation of perforin+ cells that co-expressed ThPOK (Figure 7—figure supplement 2a).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2a.

claim: Knockdown of ThPOK in differentiated CD8 T cells does not significantly influence the expression of perforin.
source: Knockdown of ThPOK in differentiated CD8 T cells did not significantly influence the expression of perforin but significantly increased the expression of granzyme B as compared to N-S shRNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 2b), suggesting that ThPOK may limit the cytotoxic function of human CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2b.

claim: Knockdown of ThPOK in differentiated CD8 T cells significantly increases the expression of granzyme B.
source: Knockdown of ThPOK in differentiated CD8 T cells did not significantly influence the expression of perforin but significantly increased the expression of granzyme B as compared to N-S shRNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 2b), suggesting that ThPOK may limit the cytotoxic function of human CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2b.

claim: ThPOK may limit the cytotoxic function of human CD8 T cells.
source: Knockdown of ThPOK in differentiated CD8 T cells did not significantly influence the expression of perforin but significantly increased the expression of granzyme B as compared to N-S shRNA (Figure 7—figure supplement 2b), suggesting that ThPOK may limit the cytotoxic function of human CD8 T cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the increased granzyme B expression upon ThPOK knockdown in CD8 T cells.

claim: The acquisition of cytotoxic function by human CD4 T cells is an integral part of the Th1 linear differentiation pathway.
source: This study demonstrates that the acquisition of cytotoxic function by human CD4 T cells is an integral part of the Th1 linear differentiation pathway.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the stepwise acquisition of cytotoxic features along the Th1 differentiation pathway.

claim: PRF1 gene expression is detected in all subsets of memory Th1 cells.
source: Several concordant observations support this conclusion. First, PRF1 gene expression was detected in all subsets of memory Th1 cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by qPCR and single-cell PCR data presented in the manuscript.

claim: The proportion of PRF1 expressing cells increases from central memory to terminally differentiated effector memory Th1 cells.
source: The proportion of PRF1 expressing cells increased from CM to terminally differentiated EM Th1 cells and this process was associated with the diversification of co-expressed TF networks.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell PCR data shown in Figure 4a.

claim: The increase in PRF1 expressing cells from CM to EM Th1 cells is associated with the diversification of co-expressed transcription factor networks.
source: The proportion of PRF1 expressing cells increased from CM to terminally differentiated EM Th1 cells and this process was associated with the diversification of co-expressed TF networks.
evidence: The claim is supported by single-cell PCR data shown in Figure 4b.

claim: The local chromatin environment at the PRF1 gene promoter becomes progressively more favorable from naive T cells to CM Th1 cells to terminally differentiated EM Th1 cells.
source: The epigenetic modifications detected at the PRF1 gene promoter reflect this increase in perforin expression and suggest that the local chromatin environment becomes progressively more favorable from naive T cells to CM Th1 cells to terminally differentiated EM Th1 cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the progressive hypomethylation and histone modification changes at the PRF1 promoter.

claim: Progressive acquisition of specific transcriptional and epigenetic marks is a hallmark of the linear differentiation model of CD4 T cell memory development.
source: Progressive acquisition of specific transcriptional and epigenetic marks is a hallmark of the linear differentiation model of CD4 T cell memory development (DEEP Consortium et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by cited literature (DEEP Consortium et al., 2016).

claim: Acquisition of cytotoxic functions by CD4 T cells follows a stepwise program similar to the linear differentiation model of CD4 T cell memory development.
source: Our work suggests that acquisition of cytotoxic functions by CD4 T cells follows a similar stepwise program.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the progressive acquisition of cytotoxic features observed in the study.

claim: The accessibility and expression of PRF1 gene in all subsets of Th1 cells provides a basis for the observation that memory Th1 cells become perforin positive and cytotoxic upon in vitro expansion.
source: The accessibility and expression of PRF1 gene in all subsets of Th1 cells also provide a basis for the classical observation that memory Th1 cells of diverse antigen-specificities that do not express the perforin protein ex vivo become perforin positive and cytotoxic upon in vitro expansion and cloning (Parronchi et al., 1992; Riaz et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the PRF1 gene accessibility data and cited literature.

claim: The in vitro acquisition of perforin expression by memory Th1 cells likely reflects pre-established PRF1 chromatin modifications in precursors of CD4CTX T cells.
source: This in vitro acquisition of perforin expression likely reflects pre-established PRF1 chromatin modifications in precursors of CD4CTX T cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the chromatin accessibility data at the PRF1 locus in Th1 cell subsets.

claim: The acquisition of cytotoxic function by human CD4 T cells is dependent on Runx3.
source: The acquisition of cytotoxic function within the Th1 lineage was promoted by Runx3 and T-bet.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments showing reduced cytotoxicity upon Runx3 knockdown.

claim: The acquisition of cytotoxic function by human CD4 T cells is promoted by T-bet.
source: The acquisition of cytotoxic function within the Th1 lineage was promoted by Runx3 and T-bet.
evidence: The claim is supported by shRNA knockdown experiments showing reduced cytotoxicity upon T-bet knockdown.

claim: Human Th1 cells acquire cytotoxic functions under the control of the master regulator Runx3 cooperating with T-bet.
source: Together these results indicate that human Th1 cells acquire cytotoxic functions under the control of the master regulator Runx3 cooperating with T-bet (Cruz-Guilloty et al., 2009; Jha et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the knockdown experiments and cited literature.

claim: Runx3 and ThPOK cross-regulate the acquisition of cytotoxic function by Th1 lymphocytes.
source: In conclusion, this study shows that Runx3 and ThPOK cross-regulate the acquisition of cytotoxic function by Th1 lymphocytes and therefore represent targets for interventions against viral infections, cancer and autoimmune disorders.
evidence: The claim is a summary conclusion supported by the knockdown experiments showing opposite effects of Runx3 and ThPOK on cytotoxic function.

claim: Runx3 and ThPOK represent targets for interventions against viral infections, cancer and autoimmune disorders.
source: In conclusion, this study shows that Runx3 and ThPOK cross-regulate the acquisition of cytotoxic function by Th1 lymphocytes and therefore represent targets for interventions against viral infections, cancer and autoimmune disorders.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the regulatory roles of Runx3 and ThPOK in cytotoxic function and is speculative regarding therapeutic applications.
